work_title: Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood

places.name: Musso & Frank Grill
places.connection: Rick Dalton and Cliff Booth have drinks and dinner; Cliff waits outside. A primary and iconic filming location.

places.name: Cinerama Dome (ArcLight Hollywood)
places.connection: Exterior shots, including the iconic marquee, contributing to the authentic 1969 Hollywood atmosphere.

places.name: Regency Bruin Theatre
places.connection: Sharon Tate and her friends watch 'The Wrecking Crew' here, a pivotal scene showing Tate's joy.

places.name: Casa Vega
places.connection: Rick Dalton meets with his agent Marvin Schwarz for dinner, discussing his career prospects.

places.name: El Coyote Cafe
places.connection: Sharon Tate, Jay Sebring, Abigail Folger, and Wojciech Frykowski have their final dinner here.

places.name: Melody Ranch Motion Picture Studio
places.connection: Primary filming location for the 'Lancer' Western scenes, including Rick Dalton's character work.

places.name: Cicada Restaurant (Oviatt Building)
places.connection: Cliff Booth picks up Pussycat (Manson Family member) outside this historic Art Deco building.

places.name: Paramount Pictures Studios
places.connection: Used for various soundstage work and backlot scenes, representing a generic Hollywood studio setting.

places.name: Former Spahn Ranch Site
places.connection: The real-world location of the Manson Family's commune, which heavily inspired the 'Spahn Movie Ranch' scenes in the film.

places.name: Former site of 10050 Cielo Drive
places.connection: The real-world tragic site that inspired the climactic events of the film. The house was recreated for filming.

places.name: Former Van Nuys Drive-In site
places.connection: Rick Dalton's movie poster for 'The 14 Fists of McCluskey' is prominently displayed on the drive-in screen.

places.name: Fox Village Theatre
places.connection: Featured in montages of Hollywood premieres and movie posters, contributing to the authentic period feel.

places.name: Hollywood Pantages Theatre
places.connection: Exterior shots used as part of the vibrant 1969 Hollywood street scenes.

places.name: Largo at the Coronet (formerly Coronet Theatre)
places.connection: Its marquee is seen advertising Rick Dalton's films, enhancing the period's cinematic landscape.

places.name: Hollywood Boulevard & Vine Street Intersection
places.connection: General street scenes and driving shots were filmed in this iconic Hollywood intersection, recreating the bustling atmosphere of 1969.
